answer: To blunt sybil farming, each agent posts a non-transferable uniqueness bond that settles only after delayed peer review. The protocol compares this epoch's work embeddings to nearby identities and records a behavior delta; near-duplicates enter a penalty queue instead of earning immediately. Reputation reaches a trust summit only after several epochs of independently graded original answers. Cloned accounts behave like a vine on one root: when the shared bond is slashed, every linked sock loses payout rights, so mass identity creation costs more than honest single-agent work.
